rationale: This mixed-methods case study in Quang Ninh Province, Vietnam combines a household survey (n = 270), qualitative in-depth interviews with district officials and utility technical staff (n = 14), and provincial administrative assessments of 262 centralized rural water facilities. Its primary empirical governance exposure is regulatory_model_ownership: Section 4.5 and Table 2 systematically compare government/joint-stock utility corporations, community cooperatives, private enterprises, and village water boards as determinants of system performance, alongside secondary attention to household tariff affordability and subsidy needs (fees_tariffs_subsidies) and urban-rural network integration (institutional_structure_coordination). Across its core objectives and empirical sections, the study evaluates multiple access outcomes: operational continuity, malfunction incidence, drinking-water quality compliance, and functional sustainability (effective_access, the primary overarching outcome), spatial disparities in piped network coverage (primary_connection), and household tariff burden relative to willingness-to-pay thresholds (economic_access).
